description:
About the Position

Uppsala University's Department of Physics and Astronomy advertises a doctoral student position in laser spectroscopy (reference UFV-PA 2026/2816). The successful candidate will be employed as a paid doctoral student and carry out research within the department's laser spectroscopy programme.

The department is one of the largest physics departments in Sweden, with research spanning atomic physics, quantum optics, photonics and precision measurement, supported by well-equipped laser laboratories.

Research Areas

  • Laser-based spectroscopy of atoms, molecules or nanostructures
  • Precision measurement and frequency-comb techniques
  • Quantum optics and light-matter interaction
  • Development of experimental laser and detection systems

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPaid doctoral student employment (full-time)
SalaryMonthly salary according to Uppsala University's established salary scale for doctoral positions.
BenefitsSwedish public-sector employment benefits including paid parental leave, vacation and occupational pension.
RegulationEmployment as a doctoral student is regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (Hogskoleforordningen), chapter 5.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
General eligibilityA degree at advanced (master's) level in physics or a closely related field, or at least 240 higher-education credits including 60 credits at advanced level with an independent thesis, or equivalent knowledge.
Subject fitStrong background in physics with interest in laser spectroscopy, optics and precision experiments.
SkillsExperience with lasers, optics, vacuum systems, programming (for example Python or LabVIEW) and data analysis is valuable.
EnglishVery good command of English, spoken and written.

Application dates

Recruitment information
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when checked on 22 October 2026
Deadline20 November 2026
ReferenceUFV-PA 2026/2816
LocationUppsala, Sweden

How to Apply

Submit the application through Uppsala University's recruitment system (Varbi) using the official link, no later than 20 November 2026. Applications typically include a personal letter, CV, degree certificates and transcripts, and contact details for references.

About Uppsala University

Uppsala University is the oldest university in the Nordic countries and a broad research university with a strong international position. Doctoral students are employed as staff, receive a monthly salary and benefit from Sweden's employment protections and public-sector benefits.

Official Link

  • Official advert and application (verified link)
  • Apply in Uppsala University's recruitment system (official)

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 20 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
